summary: Masayuki Tsukimoto is a scholar in Japanology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. Attested in 2026, he has held lecturer posts at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Massimo Pallottino was an archaeologist and historian who studied at Sapienza University of Rome (~1927–1931). He later held posts at the University of Cagliari (~1940–1945) and Sapienza University of Rome (~1946–1980).
Masumi Mochizuki works in Buddhist studies. He held posts at Minobusan University as a faculty lecturer (attested 2001), professor (attested 2015), and specially appointed professor (attested 2026).

Mathieu Boisvert works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied under Anthony Kennedy Warder and Ravindra Panth. He founded the Université du Québec à Montréal and became a professor there in 1992.

Mathurin Veyssière de La Croze worked in linguistics, history and archaeology, and Indology. In 1697 he held a post at Humboldt University of Berlin, and served as librarian and antiquary at the Royal Library of Berlin (~1697–1739).
Matteo Bartoli was a linguist who studied at the University of Vienna (~1894–1898) and under Heinrich Hübschmann. He later held a academic post at the University of Turin (~1908–1946).

Matthew B. Orsborn specializes in Buddhist studies, earning a PhD from the University of Hong Kong (–2012) under Guang Xing and Yakupitiyage Karunadasa. In 2026, he is attested as professor and head of international affairs at Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies.
Matthew Clark works in Indology and religious studies. He studied at SOAS University of London (1999–2004, PhD) under Daud Ali and George Botterill.
Matthew Immergut works in Buddhist studies and sociology. He studied under Culadasa and is attested in 2011 as an associate professor of sociology at Purchase College, State University of New York.

Matthew R. Sayers is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Texas at Austin under Joel Peter Brereton and Patrick Olivelle (attested 2008) and held a post at Lebanon Valley College (attested 2013).

Matthew Steven Mitchell works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, Osaka City University, the Inter-University Center for Japanese Language Studies, and Duke University (PhD attested 2015) under Richard M. Jaffe.

Matthew T. Kapstein is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who earned his PhD from Brown University (1980–1987). He held posts at the University of Chicago, Columbia University (~1989–1996), and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (2002).

Matthew W. King works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Toronto (–2014) under Frances Garrett, having also studied under Khenpo Kunga Sherab and Thubten Champa.

Matthias Alexander Castrén was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Helsinki and Imperial Alexander University (~1830–1836) and held academic posts there (~1851–1852).
Matthias de Vries was a linguist who studied at Leiden University (~1838–1843). He held academic posts at the University of Groningen (1849–1853) and Leiden University (1853–1891).

Matthias von Lexer was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at the University of Graz and University of Erlangen-Nuremberg. He held posts at St. Anne's Gymnasium, Kraków, and the universities of Freiburg, Würzburg, and Munich.

Matthieu Ricard is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who completed a doctorate at the Pasteur Institute under François Jacob (~1967–1972). He founded Karuna-Shechen in 2000 and served as a board member of the Mind and Life Institute.

Mattia Salvini specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at SOAS University of London (~2004–2008) under Tadeusz Skorupski and held posts at the International Buddhist College and Mahidol University (~2011).

Mauli Chand Prasad works in Buddhist studies and linguistics. He completed a doctoral dissertation at Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar Bihar University under B. Jinanand and U. Dharmaratna, and served as lecturer in Pali at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (attested 1984).
Maureen L. P. Patterson was an Indology specialist. She served as South Asia Librarian at the University of Chicago (attested in 1984 and 2007).
